To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIFs are required for the control of persistent viral infections and tumors by enhancing the effector function of CD8+ CTLs.
the central transcriptional pathway that regulates the response of CD8 T cells to hypoxia controls the effector function of CTLs during chronic infection and neoplasia.
HIFs enhance the effector function of CD8+ cytolytic T lymphocytes (CD8+ CTLs) to persistent antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hypoxia-inducing factors (HIF) in CD8+ cytolytic T cells (CTLs).
the role of HIFs and hypoxia in regulating CD8+ T cell responses and the consequences of this for the pathogenesis of persistent viral infections.
the role of hypoxia and hypoxia-indicible factors in regulating the function of cytotoxic T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIFs are a critical component of the transcriptional program that regulates the function of effector CD8+ T cell during chronic infections.
HIFs regulate the function of CD8+ CTLs during persistent infection and tumor growth.
HIFs are a major regulator of CTL function, which may have implications for the design of immunotherapies against chronic infections and tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypoxia and the HIF pathway can influence CTL effector responses to persistent antigen.
the transcriptional response to low oxygen levels in CD8+ T lymphocytes is a key regulator of the effector responses to chronic infection.
the HIFs and VHL are critical regulators of the immune response and that their dysregulation can lead to severe immunopathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIFs are important regulators of CTL effector responses, and that hypoxia and HIFs are relevant to the immunological exhaustion that occurs during chronic infection and tumor growth.
hypoxia is an important environmental factor that regulates the effector responses and immunological exhaustion of CTLs.
the transcriptional response to oxygen availability is an important mechanism for the regulation of CD8+ CTL effector function during chronic infection and tumor progression.
